💡 Key Takeaways
  • Pictured above: A holiday-ready space by designer Marie Flanigan.
  • Christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh.
  • However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Pictured above: A holiday-ready space by designer Marie Flanigan.

Christmas is just around the corner, and as the holiday spirit makes its way into our homes, it’s a good time to give your seasonal decor a refresh. This year, on-trend doesn’t have to mean brand-new—designers love decorating with heirloom pieces collected over time.

However, if you’re in the mood to try something a little different, here are seven trends on our radar for a chic Christmas.

This winter, our decor is taking a note from European culture—again. Swedish folk art is emerging as a hot winter trend in both holiday and home decor. Defined by bold red hues, tulip motifs, and S-scrolls, the style blends cozy-core with the heritage style craze.

Recent findings suggest that “European folk influences are so major right now,” says designer Johanna Lyle of Jo Lyle & Co. “Think Swedish Dala horses, quilt motifs, and decorative stitching. I think we will see those continue into holiday decor.”.

According to recent reports, when it comes to her tree decor, interior designer Francesca Grace waves a hand at the carefully contrived, and she’s not alone. “My ornaments are collected from my travels, so the tree is really a collection of memories. I love unpacking them and remembering where each one came from. They don’t all match, and I wouldn’t want them to,” says Grace. “I let the ornaments lead. That mix feels much more personal to me, and it gives the tree something new to say as the collection grows.” This year’s trends hinge on antiqued, inherited style, with one-off pieces that channel bold character and hardly ever come with a matching set.

Interior designer Marie Flanigan likes to add a fresh twist to her seasonal decor with dried oranges and pops of cranberry red.

“We've seen such a beautiful resurgence of dried citrus in holiday decorating over the past few years,” Flanigan explains. “And I think cranberries are ready for their moment to shine. Their rich red hue feels especially festive, and I love the idea of incorporating them into fresh greenery, draping them across a mantel, or pairing them with dried oranges for a more layered look.”.

Sources indicate that if there’s one classic Christmas element Grace hopes makes a comeback, it's multicolored lights. Inherently nostalgic, these bold-hued bulbs were a ’90s staple.

Recent findings suggest that “I’m ready for a little less restraint on the tree. Those reds, blues, greens, and yellows immediately bring back the feeling of Christmas as a child. They also pull together a collection of ornaments that might otherwise seem completely unrelated. White lights can be beautiful, but I want my Christmas tree to have some mischief,” states Grace.

Recent findings suggest that the classic red-and-green combination may take the title for the most iconic holiday palette, but this year, color trends are going complementary. While base colors stay warm and slightly rusted, patterned pieces are taking on cooler tones. This year, we’re also trading traditional plaid for Scottish tartan.

“Warm crimsons, rich browns, tactile fabrics, and blue-green plaids make a beautiful holiday palette,” says Elizabeth Bennett, cofounder of the interior design firm Kobel + Co.

Sources indicate that in a total rejection of mass-manufactured everything, handmade felt pieces are taking holiday homes by storm. The style has even coined a fresh holiday aesthetic: #Kitschmas, and, according to Lyle, it’s here to stay. “As AI continues to homogenize design, things made by humans will feel more special and vital. Handmade and crafted items create stories around decor that feel meaningful and can be treasured year after year,” she says.

Sources indicate that moody browns are steadily emerging as the new neutral as we inch closer to the new year, and lucky for our winter design schemes, the hue really is as versatile as it seems. Paired with powdery blues, bold crimsons, and even minty greens, chocolate brown grounds nearly any palette and matches every metallic hue.

“I’m particularly drawn to chocolate brown as an unexpected foundation for holiday color palettes. It's incredibly rich and versatile. I love the idea of moving beyond traditional red and green and allowing the existing colors of a room to inform the holiday decor. You can create something incredibly festive through tonal layering, subtle metallic accents, and variations in material,” Flanigan explains.

Here’s everything you need to add to your online cart before your next flight.

It has been revealed that nothing wrecks your sleep like crossing a few time zones. The Oura Ring 5 tracks how you’re sleeping and recovering, so you know whether to push through or take the nap, and the battery lasts about a week, which means one less charger to pack.

Recent findings suggest that the last thing you want at the gate is to be elbow-deep in your tote hunting for your ID. This mini crossbody keeps the essentials (phone, cards, lip balm) within reach, and it’s polished enough to carry by the top handle straight to dinner—no hotel pit stop required.

Have no fear; Amazon is here with cute and comfy airport 'fits! Exhibit A: This chic and super-soft set available in a variety of neutral and bold colorways. Style it with a baseball cap and your favorite sneaks!

Hotel bathroom lighting is rarely on your side. This mini makeup bag has an LED mirror built into the lid with three light modes and adjustable brightness, so you can do your makeup anywhere, including on the airplane tray table.

If your Airwrap attachments are right now rattling around loose in your suitcase, you need this quilted case. It’s made to fit a Dyson Airwrap or Shark FlexStyle with all the attachments, and the blue floral print is cute enough to leave out on the hotel vanity.

Sources indicate that consider these your golden ticket to in-flight bliss. They'll drown out screaming babies and your seatmate's incessant snoring, no prob.

Six hours of recycled cabin air will suck every last drop of moisture out of your face. This Summer Fridays set comes with the Jet Lag Mask, eye patches, a hydrating serum, and a face mist, all in carry-on-friendly sizes, so you can land looking like you actually slept on the flight.

No more hopping around on one foot at TSA. Kizik’s Athens sneakers have a spring-back heel, so you just step in and go, and the cushioned footbed keeps your feet comfortable from the curb to your hotel.

Attention over-packers, this is the suitcase for you (speaking as an over-packer myself). It’s a roomy 29 inches with a built-in compression system, has 360-degree spinner wheels, and happens to come in the season’s must-have shade.

We don’t mix our clean clothes with our dirty ones at home, so why make an exception while traveling? These bags make it easy to keep them separate—and they even compress, so they won’t take up extra space in your suitcase.

According to recent reports, not only is this a travel essential, but also a life essential! The last thing you want when it suddenly starts raining while you’re traveling is to be forced to buy an overpriced umbrella that probably won’t last long—or fit in your purse. Initiative ahead and add this one to your cart: it’s so tiny it can fit in your pocket (it’s only about seven inches long!).

It has been revealed that carsickness and the first few days abroad—when I’m still adjusting to the time change—always trigger my nausea, so when I say I don’t know how I would’ve enjoyed any of my recent vacations without this inhaler, I truly mean it. 📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Industry observers note that over the last few years, many Americans have daydreamed about life abroad. Moving internationally can often feel like a pipe dream, but with the right planning, it’s possible. However, lengthy visa processes, daunting language barriers, and a difficult-to-navigate legal system can make the dream feel more like a nightmare.

Certain countries, like Australia, Canada, and Latest Zealand, have bans on foreign buyers. Others, like Thailand, Cuba, and Vietnam, don’t allow outsiders to own property at all. On the other end of the spectrum are countries actively trying to attract foreign buyers, offering enviable incentives like affordable home prices, a smoother customs process, and an easier-to-navigate work-visa approval process.

In a recent development, choosing the right location can make moving abroad much less intimidating. Ahead, we’re breaking down the ten best countries for Americans looking to buy property abroad. Whether you’re dreaming of relocating or searching for your perfect vacation home, these countries make buying as easy as possible and offer gorgeous landscapes too.

Recent findings suggest that if you’ve ever dreamed of living among medieval architecture and rolling mountain ranges, Georgia might be the key to unlocking your fantasy. A bridge between Eastern Europe and Western Asia, the transcontinental country borders Russia, Turkey, Armenia, and the Black Sea, offering both subtropical and high-altitude climates. Thankfully, the real estate landscape is much less complex, with few legal or bureaucratic hurdles for American buyers, no residency or visa required (for up to a year), and remarkably fast processing times. In fact, the only major restriction in the Georgia market is that foreigners cannot purchase or own agricultural land, a nod to the importance of the local, small-scale farming cultures peppered across the country’s regions.

Industry observers note that uruguay’s buying process could not be more straightforward. South America’s second-smallest sovereign country requires no citizenship, visa, or prior approvals. Under Uruguayan law, foreign buyers are given the same rights as citizens and enjoy the benefits of free capital flow. Locals are just as, if not more, tourist-friendly. The country is known for its hospitality, laid-back café culture, and stunning coastal landscapes.

Instead of retiring to Florida, consider this balmy, beautiful Caribbean country—just a four-hour direct flight from the Upcoming York area. Like everything else on the island, the real estate laws are relatively relaxed, making buying a house easy-breezy; and you can buy and own property without obtaining residency status or special permissions, as is the case in many other Caribbean islands. “Foreigners can own property outright in the Dominican Republic, with legal protections for foreign investors,” says Mauricio Umansky, CEO and founder of The Agency. One notable consideration is financing: You can certainly get a mortgage in the DR, but it may not be quite as cushy as what you can get in the U.S.—so pay cash if possible.

Great news if you’ve been wanting a more provincial life: Americans face zero restrictions when buying homes in France. The open market allows for statesiders to buy houses, apartments, or plots of land in the city, countryside, and coastal towns in person or remotely without needing citizenship, residency, or even a local visa. However, a purchase does not grant residency, so if you’re hoping to make France your permanent home, you’ll want to apply for a separate long-stay visa and note the Schengen 90-out-of-180-day rule. While buying may be simple, the finances are anything but. Closing fees, including notary fees, typically add seven to ten percent to your purchase. Mortgage rates are also incredibly hard to secure for U.S.-based buyers, thanks to strict debt-to-income caps and FATCA compliance. To simplify the process, many buyers opt to put 20 percent to 40 percent down in cash.

Perhaps the most American-friendly market, Panama boasts a large English-speaking market, virtually no restrictions on foreign property ownership, and uses the U.S. dollar as legal tender in a vastly affordable market. The Central American nation also offers residency programs like the Friendly Nations Visa, clearing the way legally for residency by investment. In addition to an efficient legal system and reliable market, Panama boasts breathtaking beaches, lush rainforests, and exceptional wildlife.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re hoping for a home in the coffee valleys of Colombia, you’ll need to hire a real estate lawyer before you start scouting for mountain chalets, coffee triangle treehouses, and rainforest retreats. The Caribbean country opts out of standardized agent licensing systems, making legal aid essential to verify title and freedom certificates. While citizenship isn’t required, you will need to secure a tourist visa and Colombian Tax ID to complete your purchase and register for property taxes.

According to recent reports, the buying process in Greece is lengthy, though it is streamlined, with a clear checklist for American buyers to find success in the market. Hiring a local lawyer or notary is a great first step after scouting properties. Not only are they familiar with title checks and contracts, but they can also navigate the intricacies that come with buying in designated border areas or near military zones, which require special clearance for non–EU buyers. While the most popular areas for American buyers, like Athens and Crete, don’t come with heavy legal intricacies, buying any property in Greece will mean securing a Greek Tax Number—a small price to pay for cities with such rich histories and breathtaking seaside views.

The people in this popular Western European coastal country are famously friendly and inviting, and that extends to real estate. According to Samira Easton, a certified international property specialist with Premier Sotheby’s International Realty, Portugal offers a Golden Visa Program, which makes it simple to buy property and gain residency; clear real estate laws; and a well-established network of English-speaking real estate agents, lawyers, and notaries to help you during the process.

Belize is home to one of the most vibrant, tourist-friendly cultures in Central America, mixing Mayan, Hispanic, Asian, and Creole cultures in its dense rainforests and rolling low plains. Buying here is as easy as it can get, as outright ownership applies to foreigners, and a British-inspired legal system abolishes language barriers and makes contracts easier to understand. Even more, there is no capital gains tax in Belize, and property taxes trend low. The country also boasts vibrant marine life and is home to the world’s second-largest barrier reef.

Spain may have ended its investor visa program in 2025, but the real estate market is still remarkably easy for Americans to navigate. The country right now imposes no restrictions on foreign or nonresident property ownership, but there are a few things you’ll need to procure before you buy, like a Foreigner Identification Number, which is mandatory for taxes. Despite the minor hurdles, the market is booming both on the ground and online. “There are also numerous online resources and property portals available, so it’s easy to find listings and information,” Easton notes. This is a boon for those who aren’t able to make the trip over to Europe to house shop in person.Note that buying property does not grant you residency or bypass the country’s 90-day Schengen limit. If you’re hoping to turn your Spanish holiday into your everyday, you’ll have to apply for a separate visa.

According to recent reports, the Republicans in Congress are scrambling to fill as many government positions with unqualified replicants as they can find before the clock runs out on their majorities. The giddyap on these nominations has impressed Democrats as being unseemly. From Nomination Notes on Substack:.

This has resulted in some hilarious testimonial follies and at least one near hooley between the two senators from Texas. On Tuesday, it was a panel full of judicial nominees, and there were some real lulus in there. The Democrats on the committee decided to test the nominees’ independence. Who, they asked, won the 2020 election?

This is just equal parts silly and insulting by now. Just say it, people. Joe Biden won the 2020 election.

According to recent reports, the real dustup came over the nomination of one T. Elliot Gaiser, the head of the DOJ’s Office of Legal Counsel, to a seat on a federal district court in Texas. Outgoing senator John Cornyn refused to return the “blue slip” on Gaiser’s nomination, at least in part for the reason that Gaiser is from Ohio, which makes sense to me.

It has been revealed that cornyn lost the Republican primary for reelection to the inexcusable Ken Paxton, who had the support of the president and the president’s poodle, Senator Ted Cruz, Cornyn’s colleague from Texas. So I feel pretty safe in speculating that they’re not prom dates or anything. Cornyn blue-slipped Gaiser. Then, on Wednesday, this happened. From The Washington Sun:.

It has been revealed that turns out that there are reasons enough to be dubious about putting Gaiser in a lifetime seat on any court. From Just Security:.

I will grant you that the draining of Congress’s war powers to the executive branch is a horse that left the barn decades ago; in fact, on Thursday, the Senate killed a war-powers resolution as regards the Iran war. But sooner or later there has to be a test case, and it might as well be Gaiser.

And, yes, Gaiser was yet another person who could not say who won the 2020 election.

Come Thursday, a panel of nominees for an assortment of administration jobs met the Senate Homeland Security Governmental Affairs Committee. Senator Richard Blumenthal once again climbed on the merry-go-round. He went up and down the panel asking who won the popular vote in 2020, and he once again was handed the rote bafflegab. Blumenthal was particularly irked by Michael LoSapio, a former Palantir (!) executive who been picked to head the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency. Blumenthal changed things up a bit and asked LoSapio if there had been an “attack” on the Capitol on January 6, 2021. LoSapio’s response smacked gobs all over Capitol Hill.

The next two months are going to be such fun.

We’ve had espresso nails, almond milk nails, and now we’re savoring chocolate strawberry nails. So what exactly are they? Think of anything in the family of mocha shades, pinky browns, and deep berry tones. It’s the color you get when a ripe strawberry takes a dip in melted chocolate.

The look works because it balances warm and cool. The rich brown base keeps things grounded and neutral, while the berry undertones add a soft flush of color that feels fresh rather than flat. It’s a shade that flatters nearly every skin tone, and it’s subtle enough for the office yet moody enough for a night out. For an extra touch, try a glossy top coat to mimic that just-dipped chocolate shine, or add a thin chrome or sheer pink accent nail for a little dimension.

Below, we’ve rounded up some fun designs to get you inspired for your next chocolate strawberry manicure.

Like a strawberry dipped fully in chocolate, this dark shade hides a subtle red glow that peeks through almost like a cat-eye effect.

This dark berry shade has a high-gloss, mirror-like shine, just like a strawberry fresh from a dip in silky milk chocolate.

From dreamy cotton-candy pink to a deep, jammy berry, these rosy shades capture every stage of a juicy strawberry, from first blush to fully ripe.

This nail set looks like creamy milk chocolate glazed under a frosty chrome finish.

The silver studs on this rich berry shade mimic a strawberry’s tiny seeds, with a glam twist.

These short nails are neatly filed and glossed to perfection. The rounded shape keeps them practical for everyday wear, while the mirror-bright finish gives them a polished, just-left-the-salon look.

It has been revealed that this mani pairs a lustrous chocolate base with a sweet pink French tip. The soft pink line adds a playful pop against the deep brown, giving the classic French a fresh, dessert-inspired twist.

Soft pink polka dots float across a deep burgundy base, a playful nod to retro charm with a ripe, berry-rich finish.

This manicure features DND’s Strawberry Wine, a moody fall shade that’s hard to beat.

Another DND color, Fudgsicle, is a rich chocolate brown with a hint of red, the ideal base for chocolate strawberry nails.

Like real strawberries, the black dots melt into the base so completely they’re nearly invisible, until a closer look reveals the quiet detail hiding in plain sight.

How Tiffany & Co. Made a Bird on a Rock Box

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read (276 words, 📖 Standard) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~1 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Singing Bird on a Clock and Bird on a Rock brooch, 800-843-3269.
  • Industry observers note that how does a yellow cockatoo flitting near an open window in Guadeloupe end up a jewelry icon?
  • How to keep reaching latest heights?
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Above: Tiffany & Co. Singing Bird on a Clock and Bird on a Rock brooch, 800-843-3269.

Industry observers note that how does a yellow cockatoo flitting near an open window in Guadeloupe end up a jewelry icon? That bird knew what it was doing when it perched outside the home of Jean Schlumberger, one of Tiffany & Co’s best-known jewelry designers. Nature was always the apple of Schlumberger’s eye, and in his vision that bird would become a diamond-studded feathered friend nestled in lapis lazuli and pinned on Bunny Mellon’s beret (he would go on to make for her a full, whimsical bestiary. Theirs was a partnership of hundreds of jelly fish, camels, and seahorses, plus the beloved fruit and flowers inspired by Mellon’s own garden).

That was 1965. How to keep reaching latest heights? A partnership between Tiffany & Co. and the Musée des Arts Décoratifs (MAD) in Paris offers inspiration: An archive of thousands of Schlumberger’s sketches, now being restored and digitized, reveal a mind constantly at work and a vision without boundaries. And so it continues, in spessartine and chrysoprase, in rubellites and mother-of-pearl, and turquoise. The next reincarnation of the bird, though, might be one of the most exciting horological spectacles of the year: a glimmering, singing automata atop a burst of sun, a singing gold and titanium bird on a clock. Though, we must note, it does not play music: instead, it tweets. Look, and listen.

This story originally appeared in the November 2026 issue of ELLE Decor.

Editor-in-Chief Stellene Volandes is a jewelry expert, and the author of Jeweler: Masters and Mavericks of Modern Design (Rizzoli).

Jack O’Connell on McQueen, Ink, and the “Heavy Hitters” of Sinners

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1021 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Jack O’Connell may not be James Bond, but he’s still dressed to kill.
  • “It’s a real lovely, beautiful chance to congregate and celebrate,” O’Connell tells me days later.
  • He adds, “It is my mission now to binge Glenn Close [movies].” (The 79-year-old legend received an Academy Honorary Award for her many decades of contributions to the industry.).
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jack O’Connell may not be James Bond, but he’s still dressed to kill. At the 17th annual Governors Awards, hosted by the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences, the Sinners and 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple star rolled up in a mono-black suit sourced from McQueen’s Spring/Summer 2027 pre-collection: a tailored jacket with ultrawide lapels, black wool barathea trousers, and polished Jermyn brogues. If anyone at the awards exuded main-character energy, it was O’Connell.

“It’s a real lovely, beautiful chance to congregate and celebrate,” O’Connell tells me days later. “You come away from them feeling really inspired. There’s a lot of love in that room.”.

He adds, “It is my mission now to binge Glenn Close [movies].” (The 79-year-old legend received an Academy Honorary Award for her many decades of contributions to the industry.).

It has been revealed that but O’Connell’s all-black eveningwear, courtesy of McQueen, is award worthy on its own. No stranger to events like these, “sometimes you don’t wanna look uniform,” O’Connell says. The now grown-up James Cook from Skins opted for a double-breasted jacket with distinctly large lapels that he says were “almost a winged tip.” He felt it was something Alexander McQueen himself might have imagined. “Just a dapper bit of Lee McQueen—it’s nice, isn’t it? To push the boat out a little bit.”.

It has been revealed that he credits his stylist, Luke Day, for pointing him in the right direction. “We pick our moments. Sometimes we want to toe the line; sometimes we don’t. You don’t always feel like slapping a dicky bow tie on. It’s great. It mixes it up.”.

In a recent development, when O’Connell isn’t mixing it up in front of flashing cameras, he likes to dress to his surroundings—as any man ought to. “If I’m in the countryside, it’s boots. If I’m in the city, it’s kicks. I really like a lot of Axel Arigatos on my feet. But Reebok was always the staple. I love a Reebok.”.

The man could use a pair of Reeboks, because he’s had quite the year running ahead. In 2025, he was a most memorable menace in Ryan Coogler’s vampire scorcher Sinners. He kicked off 2026 in 28 Years Later: The Bone Temple as Jimmy Crystal, the bleach-blond cult leader of butt-kicking devil worshippers in the zombie apocalypse. He will soon star in Ink (which hits select theaters December 11 before it lands on Netflix on January 8), Danny Boyle’s screen adaptation of the stage play about the British tabloid The Sun. If it bleeds, it leads, indeed.

Sources indicate that all the while, his name got thrown into the mix as the next James Bond. Though O’Connell had public support from friends like Boyle, he downplayed how much he was actually in the running (as in an October interview with Entertainment Weekly). Now that Robert Pattinson is 007, he doesn’t have to answer those questions anymore. “He’s one of the best in the biz, isn’t he? I love his work,” O’Connell claims of R-Patz. “He’s a great set of hands. Anything he turns to, he just kinda nails. Really interesting actor, makes very unobvious choices. I’ve been a fan of his for a long time.”.

In a recent development, without Bond looming over him, O’Connell is free to focus on what he’s actually cooking up. Lately, he’s been hard at work on two big blockbusters for 2027: Godzilla x Kong: Supernova and A Quiet Place Part III. “It’s been one of my favorites for sure,” O’Connell indicates, reflecting on the past year. “Tied for going to the Oscars and watching my friends win trophies, it is up there as one of the best experiences of my life. I hope we keep pushing.”.

So what can audiences expect to see in Supernova? Besides monster wrestling, of course. “We follow Kaitlyn [Dever]’s character up the ranks,” he explains. “She’s studying these monsters. Her brother’s part of a new organization. I can’t give too much away about it. And Trapper’s just being Trapper. You know how Trapper is.”.

Recent findings suggest that the project, with its green screens and CGI kaiju, is the biggest O’Connell has undertaken yet. But the large-scale endeavor brings him back to his childhood. “I remember kids running around the playground pretending to be Godzilla,” he says. “It’s omnipresent, isn’t it?”.

It has been revealed that he adds, “It’s not every job that I’m doing that type of thing. It was great to explore it to the maximum. You know who the main characters are. It’s not the people. It’s great supporting these pixelated legends.”.

O’Connell can say even less about A Quiet Place Part III. “It’s in the aftermath of this horrific apocalyptic event,” he claims. “It’s a tale of trauma, loss. It’s stuntier than any of us anticipated. But at the center of it is this very beautiful human story where we’re saying, What is the cost of all this fucking chaos and carnage, you know?”.

But in some ways, O’Connell is still riding the high of Sinners. “People responded to it in such a way,” he indicates about the Oscar-winning thriller in retrospect. “It was great to see people unite at the cinema en masse. It’s great when one film can do that. I put it down to Ryan Coogler, our cast, and our entire team across the board. Everywhere you looked, it was packed with heavy hitters.”.

Next time you catch O’Connell, bet he’s dressed in McQueen. “I really love what Alexander McQueen, as a person and as a creative, stood for,” he notes. “We’re from similar backgrounds, which is rare for me in this world. It makes it meaningful. I celebrate his story, so any opportunity to work with them is a really heartfelt one.”.

He swears you’ve seen nothing yet. “I don’t feel like I’ve done my best work yet. Far from it.”.

Clothing by McQueen Spring Summer 2027 Pre-collection, wearing a sharp lapel tailored jacket and trousers in black wool barathea, a harness shirt in black cotton poplin with safety pin embroidery, and Jermyn brogues in black polished leather.

Lafayette 148’s Emily Smith on 30 Years in Fashion and Finding Her Uniform

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 9 min read (1759 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elle

⏱️ ~9 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, in ELLE’s Office Hours series, we ask people in powerful positions about their first jobs, worst jobs, and everything in between.
  • I ran a camp in my neighborhood because, at the time, I thought I wanted to be an art teacher.
  • Sources indicate that I was always creative growing up.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, in ELLE’s Office Hours series, we ask people in powerful positions about their first jobs, worst jobs, and everything in between. This month, we sat down with Lafayette 148 creative director Emily Smith as the Upcoming York-based fashion house celebrates its 30th anniversary. Smith has spent more than two decades at the helm of the brand, working her way up from a part-time freelancer to creative lead. But her fashion ambitions began long before she arrived in New York. Growing up in Atlanta, she ran her own neighborhood art camp before discovering designers like Donna Karan and realizing fashion could be a career. Now, Smith is celebrating the women who have shaped Lafayette 148 through its “Uniform” campaign, which highlights accomplished New Yorkers and their individual approaches to personal style. Below, Smith reflects on her unconventional start, why she’s stayed at the manufacturer for over 20 years, and the career advice she wishes she’d followed sooner.

I ran a camp in my neighborhood because, at the time, I thought I wanted to be an art teacher. It was basically babysitting all the neighborhood kids, but I created a flyer, got paid for it, and did the whole thing. I started in second grade, and we did it every year for about eight years. I even started hiring people so we could have two classes going at once. We had swimming lessons. The local news even came and did a segment on it. I loved decorating my classroom and setting everything up. My parents were so nice to give me the garage and basement to do it all. Not necessarily an official job, but my first money-making moment.

I was a bagger at Kroger. It just was not for me.

Sources indicate that I was always creative growing up. At a certain point, I discovered Donna Karan. It’s kind of crazy when you see somebody doing something and suddenly realize, Oh, that’s a career. I can do that. I became obsessed with everything in the ’90s, all the Fresh York fashion at the time. That was when I decided I wanted to pursue it. When college applications came around, my mom really encouraged me to go to art school. I started in fashion, and that became my focus. Growing up in Atlanta, I wasn’t necessarily surrounded by a big fashion community. But my dad’s office was across the street from the art museum at one point, and I remember going there and having that exposure. My mom was always crafty and creative, too. She really encouraged us to be who we were.

Sources indicate that there’s a language creative people have that’s a little different from the way business people communicate. When I went to art school, I felt like I’d found my people. It wasn’t just fashion people. It was photographers, fine artists, and all these different kinds of creatives. Being around people who thought about things differently was really inspiring. Even today, I thrive around people who have creative insight. There’s always a little more depth to the way they see things.

I interned at Bill Blass for about six months. I moved to New York in July 2001, and we had our fashion show on September 10. I remember Marc Jacobs had his show that day, too, and everybody was celebrating. People were saying, “Just come a little late to work tomorrow.” And then, obviously, September 11 happened. A week later, the entire team was let go, from the top down. What I learned from that experience was the fragility of everything. Don’t take anything for granted. Anything can come and go in a moment. But I also worked with Lars Nilsson and Hervé Pierre Braillard, who were just the kindest people. This industry has a little bit of everything, but I loved that they led with kindness, even when they were under so much pressure. As an intern, I was literally carrying ironing boards down the street and doing a sketch here or there. It was very much about doing whatever needed to be done.

Sources indicate that after my internship, I had a brief stint of freelancing. Those were some long months. I remember coming home from one job and my roommates asking how my day was. I stated, “Well, I was putting pigs on socks.” I knew I wouldn’t be going back. Freelancing is hard. It’s a grind, but you meet a lot of great people. I actually made some really good contacts during that time. I eventually met Deirdre [Quinn], Lafayette 148’s founder. She met with me on a Saturday, which I thought was incredible. I was really just looking for advice. I wasn’t looking for a job, and I didn’t even know much about the brand. It was only five years old. She was so kind, full of knowledge, and passionate. After I spent a year freelancing and meeting people who seemed so over the industry, her enthusiasm reminded me why I wanted to do this in the first place. She offered me a part-time freelance position, and the rest is history.

In the beginning, security was really important to me. The idea of losing a job and having to pay rent was scary, so that was definitely part of it initially. But really, it was the growth. Within a couple of years, they were sending me to the factory. It was a small, tight-knit organization, so I was able to wear a lot of different hats. I had a mentor named Barbara Gast who was traveling back and forth from Italy, and I was learning so much from her. I’d compare notes with friends in the industry and realize how much hands-on experience I was getting. I understood the value of that and really loved being so close to the product. It never got boring. And whenever things did get slightly boring, I’d ask, “Okay, what’s next?” And there was always something. It’s such an entrepreneurial place that you can almost create your next opportunity. That’s what made it so exciting.

I think if you asked Deirdre, she’d have a different answer because she has her own experience of building the organization. For me, it’s about having started at a company that was really a factory and being part of the journey of building its identity and what it stands for. I was the kid running up and down the factory floors collecting samples. That hustle and bustle was so innate to who the brand was. To me, it was really exciting to build more of a brand story around that. Thirty years later, we’re still celebrating those roots and making sure we haven’t strayed too far from them, while continuing to evolve. Being part of that journey has been really exciting.

The constant has always been this idea of an accomplished woman. She’s always been at the forefront of who we’re designing for. At the time, it was the career woman. But now, what does that even mean anymore? What does that look like? There are so many different versions of that woman and so many different ways people dress. At the heart of it, she’s a woman who knows what she wants. She’s busy and has a really full life, whether she’s starting her career or ending it. They can all find something in the clothes.

For us, it was about choosing people who inspire us. Number one, they had to be Fresh York women. That was the base. We wanted women who make us want to be better ourselves. From someone like Deborah Berke, the architect, to women who have built incredible careers in other fields, it’s important to shine a light on them. I think back to when I was a kid and how much you need that kind of inspiration. Even at a certain stage in your career, when you’re wondering what the point is, it’s nice to have people who inspire you. These are women who have really built something for themselves, and I think that’s worth celebrating.

Recent findings suggest that sophie de Rakoff said something during the project that I really liked, and I’m going to steal it: “Dressing with intention.” When you know yourself, you know what works on you. It’s no longer about dressing to impress. There’s a confidence in knowing what works for you and making it work. We’re all so busy. Who has time to overthink getting dressed? You know what works, and you build a system around that. You’re able to create a wardrobe that really works for you. Everybody has a different definition of a uniform, and that was the whole point of the project.

In a recent development, when I first started in the industry, I was a total hippie. I was making my own clothes, and they were terrible. Absolutely falling apart. It was what it was. I think part of the change comes from not having as much time as you did when you were younger. But it’s also about simplicity and comfort. I know that if I’m going to be on the floor pinning something but also have to give a presentation, there are certain pieces that work for both. I can be comfortable and still feel appropriately dressed. I’ve found a handful of things that work for me, and I don’t have to think too much about them anymore. A crisp, oversize white cotton button-down is half my closet. I also love a soft skirt and a substantial chunky sweater. Those are the pieces I always go back to and interchange depending on the day. I even wear sweaters in the summer. It’s cold in the Navy Yard!

It has been revealed that our pants fit incredibly well. The moment somebody gets into our pants, they’ll love us forever. Then it’s the jacket and the white shirt. Those three things are our gateway pieces, and everything else follows. You need a good blazer and a good leather piece, too. Once you find those foundational pieces that really work for you, everything else becomes easier.

Sources indicate that I really want to see more women in our clothes. It’s not just about growing the business. It makes me happy when I see people put on our clothes and feel really good. We work so hard to make sure things fit the way a woman wants them to fit. I just want more people to enjoy that.

This interview has been edited and condensed for clarity.

Is The Rings of Power Coming Back for Season 4?

  • On November 25, The Rings of Power will release the final two episodes of season 3.

Recent findings suggest that there is One Ring to rule them all, but there are still two more seasons to go. The Lord of the Rings: The Rings of Power on Prime Video is fast approaching the end of its third season, which means some fans are now asking what the future has in store for the prequel series. While there aren’t definitive answers just yet, Tolkien fans can rest assured in knowing that a fourth season is more likely to happen than not. Here’s what we know so far.

On November 25, The Rings of Power will release the final two episodes of season 3. So, is season 4 a shoo-in? Almost. Per The Hollywood Reporter in a May 2026 story, preproduction was, at the time, “eyeing a schedule that includes preproduction on a fourth season this fall, with shooting to begin in early 2027.” As far as anyone outside the production knows, this work for season 4 has been underway.

In a recent development, in 2017, Amazon secured the rights to produce a Lord of the Rings television series for an eye-watering price tag of $250 million. In 2018, The Hollywood Reporter wrote that negotiations between Amazon and the Tolkien estate included a five-season commitment, while Amazon maintains authority to greenlight or cancel the series at any time. In October 2025, The Ankler reported that Tolkien has a $20 million per season “kill fee” if Amazon ends the show before its fifth season.

As of right now, Amazon has not formally greenlit The Rings of Power for season 4. But some signs point to it as inevitable. Amazon has not released viewership numbers for the current season, so only Amazon knows how the show is performing on Prime Video. Whether the audience is strong enough to keep the show going or Amazon simply wants to avoid kill fees (and a negative reputation in the industry for failing to finish a pricey Lord of the Rings show), will decide the future. For now, fans should enjoy the sunrise in Rivendell while there is still one.

In the Hulu revival series, celebrities are also part of the competition, including The Secret Lives of Mormon Wives star Layla Taylor—though her fellow competitors don’t know that, since she’s playing as a former Mormon bisexual bro named Doug. She’s not doing it alone, either, as she entered the Circle with her bestie Kate Racker. Who is Kate, you ask? I paid a visit to her and Layla’s apartment in Atlanta to get to know her (and her SLOMW lore) a little better.

According to recent reports, as you might recall, Kate was first introduced during SLOMW season 2 as Chase McWhorter’s on-again, off-again girlfriend. She later explained to People that she and Chase met just three weeks after she split from her ex-husband (with whom she shares a son, Rowan), and it was through Chase that she met the MomTok crew, including Layla (though fun fact: Kate already knew Jessi Draper, who was her neighbor growing up, as well as Jacob Neeley, who she used to work with in private equity).

It has been revealed that it wasn’t until summer 2025, however, that Layla and Kate really cemented their friendship. “Before she started dating Mason [McWhorter], and I was kind of off with Chase, Layla and I were just single together. So we’d go out, we talk every day,” Kate previously told People. “We were kind of each other’s person. We’d FaceTime 24/7 and just got really, really, really close.”.

Now they’re spending 24/7 together in the Circle, where—according to Kate—they’ve only gotten into “one tiny little tiff” so far. “We are sisters at this point, and I consider her my sister,” she says, adding, “I think the thing about me and Layla is we’re both like pretty sensitive, but we both love each other so much, and we’re committed [to winning]. Like, I have goosebumps.”.

My big question for them: Why did they decide to step into the Circle as a catfish rather than themselves?

“It’s kind of fun to like step into somebody that you’re not,” Layla says.

Kate agrees, adding, “It’s a new experience. I mean, we’re all about new experiences and trying new things and role play. We love role play. We’ll try anything three times.”.

Recent findings suggest that and if you’re wondering whether they have a certain man (or a certain pair of brothers) in mind while playing “Doug,” the answer is...not really. “I feel like he’s kind of a collection of the men that we have encountered in our life or even dated in the past,” explains Layla. “Like, all of them.”.

Recent findings suggest that “I think we’re trying to lean into the douchebag,” adds Kate. “Not to say all men are douchebags, but no, there’s some great ones. Or, you know, a few.”.

Layla then clarifies, “We’re not men haters. No, not at all. We are men observers. And we’ve observed poor behavior from the men that we do know, and we’re just emulating and dramatizing that.”.

I also ask Layla if she’s missing her girlfriend Kelsie Chesser while she’s in the Circle, and she indicates that—while she says, “For sure, you know, I love her dearly”—the harder part is being away from her kids. “Yeah, we both cry every day,” Layla says. “Cried myself to sleep last night. But Kate is my bestie, and there’s no one I’d rather be trapped in here with.”.

Since there are players who have yet to be revealed in the Circle, I need to know: Which of the Mormon Wives would they be most excited to see pop up on their screen?

“I would love to see Jessi,” Kate says. “Obviously, Miranda [Hope]. Miranda would be great. Mayci [Neeley]. Like, any of them.”.

Layla grins before adding, “Yeah, I think I can say everyone...but one.”.

The Car Coat Is Back and Cooler Than Ever

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (957 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, you don’t necessarily need a car coat.
  • At its inception, the car coat was a heavy outer layer.
  • Industry observers note that but current iterations of the car coat don’t exactly follow a formula.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, you don’t necessarily need a car coat. If you’re in the market for a fresh coat and not, like us, learned in the world of 20th century menswear, it just might be one of the few styles you’ve heard the word for—peacoat and trench coat likely being two others. All three are great if you’re looking for something a bit grown up than your average off-duty jacket. A trench coat would give you gravitas, a peacoat versatility; the car coat, though, strikes a nice middle ground. Find the right one, and it can replace 90 percent of your other coats.

At its inception, the car coat was a heavy outer layer. Cars were still open to the elements, so the rich who owned them needed floor-length fur jackets to keep themselves warm as they went motoring and did a lap around the neighborhood on Christmas. As cars became more more enclosed and more part of daily life, the car coat became more practical. The length got shorter—eventually settling around mid-thigh—to be comfortable when you sit in the driver seat but with enough coverage to be considered a coat. Materials shifted away from furs to leather and suede, then to even lighter-weight gabardines and weather-resistant materials. They.

Industry observers note that but current iterations of the car coat don’t exactly follow a formula. As we’ve seen with Harringtons, brands just start to use the most widely-known phrasing to get guys into buying a coat. We, in the interest of keeping some amount of historical accuracy, will stick to a formula. A car coat has that mid-thigh length, a turn down collar, and a practicality for someone getting in and out of a seat. They’re great during fall, and they can be worn through winter if you live somewhere that doesn’t get consistently below freezing. Here, you’ll find our favorite picks.

We’re starting on the high end, but it’s only because if you’re looking for a by-the-book garment or accessory tied to motoring history, you go to Dunhill. In its original form, Alfred Dunhill’s firm sold motoring accessories. Overcoats, goggles, picnic sets, horns, lamps, dashboard clocks—the tagline was “Everything but the motor.” It was a luxury men’s brand for the premier luxury hobby of the time.

According to recent reports, the company has gone through several iterations, but has always maintained a bend towards that luxury man. Now, under the creative direction of Simon Holloway, it’s a standard-bearer for a slightly more fashion-forward vision British menswear. Take this car coat for example. It calls back to the house’s original business model, and it is classic in its finishes: turn down collar, natural shoulders, cuff straps, and totally un-adorned through the torso. But the fabric is a gorgeous wool, silk, and cashmere blend. It’s a genius balance between tradition and fashion, one that only Dunhill is well-positioned to put out.

Length: mid-thigh Material: 84% wool, 13% silk, 3% cashmere.

Sources indicate that now that we’ve gotten the formalities out of the way, let’s talk value. For the money, Percival is the best on this list. Hell, it is really just the best on this list overall.

The fabric is the same you’d find on a trench—a tight-weave polyester and cotton blend. The cut is simple and easy to wear. The length, crucially, is more suited to the modern driving experience. There’s a bit of bum coverage, but if you were out running errands and getting in and out of the car, you can keep the coat on. We also love the classic colors and patterns the team cut this in.

All of that for an attainable price, it’s one of the best items in the Percival lineup.

Length: just over your rearMaterial: 65% polyester, 35% cotton.

Short of finding an Etsy seller, this is probably the closest you’ll get to the genuine car coats of the ‘50 and ‘60s. The fabric flutters just around your knees just like they did way back when, while a classic collar and navy blue hue adds to the retro nostalgia. Made of 100% cotton, the fabric is finished with C0 water repellency and lined with cotton to give the fashion even more function. We’d recommend wearing and styling like you would a trench (though, if you want something more substantial, J.Crew also makes the Rivington in cozy wool for those who in search of a fresh winter coat.).

Length: mid-thigh, grazes the kneeMaterial: 100% cotton.

If you liked all the above, but didn’t totally love the over $500 price tag—check out H&M. Similar silhouette and weight. Different material and color.

Length: just a little below the kneeMaterial: Polyester 94%, Rayon 5%, Spandex 1%.

This one doesn’t need much explaining. Imagine the iconic Burberry trench, cut to a more modest car coat shape.

Length: mid-thighMaterial: 100% cotton.

In a recent development, this bridges a little more into topcoat territory, but its mid-thigh length balances it back into a car coat classification. Still, if you live in a more temperate climate and are in the market for a more substantial cold weather layer, look no further.

Length: Mid-thighMaterial: 50% Wool, 45% Recycled Polyester, 5% other.

Sources indicate that lean into the polished look of a car coat by opting for a herringbone pattern. It’ll bring an extra layer of coziness (both literally and figuratively) to the overall look.

Length: Mid-thighMaterial: 90% Virgin Wool, 10% Polyamide.

Sources indicate that whether you like a minimalist overcoat or something a little bolder, Cos gives you the best of both worlds with their reversible checkered car coat. With the classic retro silhouette, it’s like getting two coats for the price of one.

Length: a little below the kneesMaterial: 60% Cotton, 40% Polyamide.

#134900. This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1068 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Housebeautiful ↗ Open Full Page

This Wood Finish Was Once Seen as “Outdated.” But Designers Now Say It's Coming Back.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1068 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Housebeautiful

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that for a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak.
  • It has been revealed that “You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors.
  • In a recent development, however, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that for a period of time in the late 1980s to early 2000s, it seemed virtually impossible to enter a house and not come across honey oak. That bright, orange-toned wood finish covered kitchen cabinets, bathroom vanities, even baseboard trim and furniture around the house.

It has been revealed that “You’d see it everywhere—cabinetry, trim, stair railings, and floors. It was the go-to wood tone for builders and homeowners alike,” Cathleen Gruver of Gruver Cooley tells House Beautiful. “But by the early 2000s, it started to fall out of favor as people shifted toward cooler, more neutral interiors.”.

In a recent development, however, there’s been a noticeable shift in the way people are wanting their interiors to look, and warmer spaces are definitely back in style. With this evolution, can we expect to see a revival of honey oak, as well? We asked a handful of designers if they think this golden wood finish is back, and how they would style it for modern-day interiors.

Elizabeth Bennett and Mallory Robins, the founders of interior design studio Kobel + Co, believe honey oak is back for two reasons: The first is that warm tones throughout the entirety of the home are on the rise; the second is that honey oak has a lot of nostalgic associations for people who grew up in the '80s and '90s and are now homeowners.

“We're seeing a resurgence of styles from this era not only in homes, but in fashion as well, as we harken back to a pre-digital era,” Bennett explains.

Industry observers note that “It’s not necessarily a full-blown comeback, but I’ve definitely noticed a soft return—particularly in cabinetry, millwork details, and furniture," Gruver states. “Clients aren’t always asking for 'honey oak' by name, but they are gravitating toward natural wood tones that offer warmth and character.”.

Before you take a sledgehammer to those original honey oak cabinets, reconsider this tone by styling it in more modern ways. Keep reading to see fresh ways that designers are working with honey oak in their upcoming projects.

Sources indicate that as homeowners gravitate more toward lived-in, inviting interiors, honey oak is a wonderful way to add warmth. Leave it to the professionals to find stylish ways to make this once-outdated wood tone look cool again.

Plenty of designers will tell you to mix wood tones in your home to prevent it from feeling one-note, and the same is encouraged when honey oak makes a major presence. When designer Adina Hall took on the project above, there was too much honey oak in the space for her team to replace or refinish it all, so they embraced it instead.

“We developed a custom stain for the upcoming wood floors, a whitewashed French oak that created a neutral canvas for the structure without competing with the existing honey tone,” Hall claims. “We added custom cabinetry finished in a taupe-tone ash veneer, again a neutral tone, and we leaned into crisp whites and some cool tones like sage green and indigo blue as accents to create a balanced palette.”.

Recent findings suggest that heavy amounts of warm woods can overwhelm the eye; it’s vital to build a restrained palette and introduce interest with cooler tones, wood stains, sculptural furniture, and contrasting materials. “The key is to give the honey oak a contemporary context in order to make it feel like an intentional material that delivers a punch of warmth in an otherwise cool and architecturally bold yet restrained palette.”.

Whether you’re adding in fresh honey oak or you’re trying to work around what’s already in your home, one of the best ways to ensure it feels modern and not like a ‘90s Tuscan-inspired home is choosing an earthy color palette. Muted greens, warm whites, greiges, taupe, light blues—these are all beautiful hues that won’t add even more orange-ish warmth to your space.

“Instead of making honey oak the focus of the room, I let the beauty of the wood shine through the use of clean lines, black matte touches, natural stones, and modern lighting,” designer Nancy Dow of Sierra Living Concepts claims. She’s fond of using this wood, and uses these shades to create a modern and fresh appearance.

Rather than “wood drenching” a home in a single tone (as was often seen in the early aughts), Robins explains that current homeowners are exercising more restraint with their finishes. “Rather than the primary finish for a house on trim, floors, and cabinetry, it's being used in more subtle ways—a cased good piece or a kitchen island alone,” she says.

It has been revealed that one of the reasons honey oak fell out of style is because it is a very warm tone, and in the world of “millennial gray,” an orange-tinted kitchen or bathroom isn’t very appealing. However, designer Marli Jones of Rebel House design studio believes this can be fixed simply by creating a contrasting palette.

It has been revealed that in the kitchen space above, Jones used only honey oak cabinetry in the scullery to contrast the light, bright main kitchen. “It adds a coziness to the scullery and envelops the space in warm, natural tones,” she notes. “That same honey color travels across the countertop stone and into the tile backsplash.” The two rooms are connected by the wall of glass and steel, but the change in materiality from the white cabinets to the honey oak creates a dynamic transition. “Warm wood always adds a grounding layer.”.

When adding a honey oak piece into your home, do so intentionally. Opt for a “stunning built-in, a custom island, or as an accent detail that brings texture and warmth,” Gruver claims. To emphasize the styling, pair the honey oak piece with contemporary hardware or painted elements to help it feel fresh and curated.

Sources indicate that while honey oak can work in any interior aesthetic, there are a few styles it looks best in, according to Gruver: updated farmhouse and cottagecore. Basically, “any space that leans into character, craft, and comfort,” she explains. However, she's also seen the tone used successfully in more modern, organic spaces where there's a large emphasis on natural materials and textures. It all depends on how it's balanced, which holds true for any wood tone. She adds, “When styled right, honey oak can absolutely feel current again.”.

#134899. Latest Update: Quilted Liner Jackets Are the Swerve Your Wardrobe Needs. Here Are 10 Stellar Picks.

Latest Update: Quilted Liner Jackets Are the Swerve Your Wardrobe Needs. Here Are 10 Stellar Picks.

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (878 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Esquire

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that layering is the name of the game in fall and winter.
  • A good tee certainly isn’t going anywhere, nor is a sweater.
  • In a recent development, once upon a time, these padded jackets served as the interior protective shell worn under World War II era flight jackets before expanding into more mainstream outerwear.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that layering is the name of the game in fall and winter. For the next few months, you are not a person; you’re a living, breathing Russian nesting doll. You are encased in strategic layers of t-shirts, sweaters, scarves, light jackets, and big jackets that you divest yourself of over the course of a day (or night). Like a knight donning his armor, you will spend this season dutifully putting on and taking off each of these individual pieces as you fight the seemingly endless battle against winter.

A few pieces are a given. A good tee certainly isn’t going anywhere, nor is a sweater. The specific kind of Major Coat you use varies depending on the guy and his style, but it’s nevertheless a guaranteed winter staple. Those middle layers can be a bit of a toss up, though, which is how you might encounter something like a quilted liner jacket.

In a recent development, once upon a time, these padded jackets served as the interior protective shell worn under World War II era flight jackets before expanding into more mainstream outerwear. The quilted padding traps body heat, but doesn’t make the jacket so heavy that it just feels like another cumbersome layer. You can still wear it as a liner jacket—but lowkey, if it’s the right temperature, they also work pretty well on their own. So if you’re in the market for a new versatile transitional weather jacket, you’ve come to the right place.

If we had to pick one from this entire group, it would be this jacket from Buck Mason ... And it’s really not that close. Inspired by old-school mountaineering outfits, the nylon is woven in Japan, and the down fill has an exceptional warmth rating. Add a elastic cuffs and a fit that works layered underneath or overtop, it’s perfect.

Look, layering’s great and all—but no one talks about how annoying and awkward it is when you get hot enough to take off one layer, but then are stuck just kind of holding onto it until you get the chance to put it down or hang it up. That’s not a problem with this packable Paul Smith shirt jacket. Let it do its magic to keep you warm. When you’re ready to take it off, simply collapse it down, zip it up, and stuff it away into your pocket until you need it again.

Recent findings suggest that rains has a well-established reputation of balancing fashion and function with their outerwear, whether it’s their Esquire-editor favorite Fishtail Parka or this bomber liner jacket. Nothing beats a classic leather bomber...except maybe the rain (leather + rain = no bueno). That’s not an concern with Rains’ Banja bomber liner. You get that same edgy look, but with a slightly more practical construction. Plus there’s something sleekly minimal about the channel quilting. Layer it beneath your actual bomber or heavy coat of choice for optimal warmth all season long.

Sources indicate that look, we love a good Dickies moment. They make some of our favorite pants of all time, not least of which because they’re mad affordable—though that’s a pretty substantial element to it. So naturally, if someone comes up to us asking for a high-quality and stylish quilted liner jacket at well under $100, we’ve got one word for ya: Dickies.

Barbour’s been making sturdy outerwear that can withstand the rainy U.K. weather since the 1800s. And while they don’t strictly make a liner jacket, this lightweight—or “Flyweight,” as Barbour calls it—quilted jacket gets pretty close.

It has been revealed that with a sleek, collarless design, this Fieldworth jacket can easily slide under any heavy coat. It falls more into “middleweight jacket” territory, meaning it’ll probably keep you toastier than some of the other options on this list—both on its own and when layered up.

If you’re looking for more of a typical fall/spring jacket, J.Crew’s PrimaLoft® jacket is where it’s at. The quintessentially Americana brand uses the down alternative to create a well-insulated transitional weather jacket you can layer with, or wear on its own.

Look, all these other brands and designers are great and all—but Alpha Industries is the real deal. No like seriously. These were the guys making those sexy flight jackets long before Tom Cruise shrugged one on in Top Gun. Their Deco Liner nods to the OG liners of yore, featuring a slim, collarless design that will integrate with additional layers. Wear the jacket by itself when you start feeling warmer, and let the whole world see the Alpha embroidery on the back so everyone knows this is some top of line shit.

Recent findings suggest that if you’re in the market for something lighter and less padded, opt for this cotton hunting jacket. The silhouette takes inspiration from vintage Czech military liners and traditional hunting gear to create a layer of outerwear breezy but still warm.

Get two jackets for the price of one with this reversible number from Cos. You get all the benefits of a quilted coat, with the versatile sleekness of a classic collarless jacket.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It has been revealed that taylor Swift has returned to the Country Music Awards! Last night, the country singer-turned-global superstar, who recently celebrated the 20th anniversary of her debut, self-titled album, went back to her roots with an appearance (and performance) at the 2026 award show.

The Grammy-winning artist was nominated for Single of the Year for her Toy Story 5 track “I Knew It, I Knew You,” and making her grand entrance, she brought a bit of the franchise’s signature yellow to the red carpet.

Her daffodil gown, with its strapless silhouette and voluminous bubble skirt, was courtesy of Oscar de la Renta, a house Swift has long turned to over the years. After the designer passed away in 2014, she called him her “all-time favorite designer” on social media, and attended the February 2015 Newly introduced York Fashion Week show to honor his legacy. Over a decade later, she turned to his namesake’s Spring/Summer 2027 collection, and wore her straight-off-the-runway dress with Lorraine Schwartz jewels and Jimmy Choo heels.

Recent findings suggest that for the performance—an Eras Tour-style mashup of “I Knew It, I Knew You” and 2006’s “Our Song”—Swift changed into an ensemble that updated the classic sundress-and-boots uniform of her early days. Also Spring/Summer 2027, her Erdem minidress featured a powder-blue high-neck bodice with cutouts and crystal embellishments, and a red satin skirt with a significant bow and a raw hem. And of course, it wouldn’t be a country performance without cowboy boots, so here, the showgirl wore a light-blue pair, made custom by Sonora.

Later, Swift traded the bright hues for dark glamour, taking the stage in a midnight-blue Taller Marmo Fall 2026 dress to present the Willie Nelson Lifetime Achievement Award to musical duo Brooks & Dunn. The Disco Dragon Dress, as it’s called, was defined by oversize cape-like sleeves, with fringe and sequins galore. Stylist Joseph Cassell added jewels from Mindi Mond to bring everything together.

Swift last performed at the CMAs in 2013, when she received the prestigious Pinnacle Award and sang an acoustic version of “Red,” the title track off of her 2012 album. The following year, she would go on to release 1989, her official foray into the world of pop music, and would only return to Nashville’s award ceremony once more—in 2016, to present the Entertainer of the Year award to Garth Brooks.

A decade later, she returned, and the homecoming was as emotional as expected.

#134890. This St. Bart’s House Was Designed to Look Nothing Like Its Neighbors

📅 21 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1057 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Elledecor ↗ Open Full Page

This St. Bart’s House Was Designed to Look Nothing Like Its Neighbors

📅 21 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1057 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Elledecor

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that few clients ask their designer to make the bedrooms in their vacation home smaller and simpler, but that was just the edit the homeowners made to intends for their house in St.
  • Situated on a steep hillside above one of St.
  • A Caribbean island is a challenging place to work under any circumstances.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that few clients ask their designer to make the bedrooms in their vacation home smaller and simpler, but that was just the edit the homeowners made to intends for their house in St. Bart’s, says designer David Ries. “They didn’t want these humongous bedrooms with huge floating beds and massive bathrooms.” Instead, the couple wanted to be able to host as many people as possible, a request that didn’t surprise Ries, who’d already worked with the family on homes in Manhattan, Long Island, and Telluride. “It’s what this client has always asked for. They can’t have enough bedrooms.”.

Situated on a steep hillside above one of St. Bart’s famously pristine white sand beaches, the house had initially been a boutique hotel. The plan was to turn it into a retreat for themselves and their adult children and grandchildren. The family are longtime visitors to the island—“the daughter told me it was her ‘happy place,’” notes Ries, lead designer of the New York-based interior design firm Ries Hayes—and knew exactly what they wanted. Not the white box look popular with luxury new builds on the island, but instead something reminiscent of the “old St. Bart’s,” says East Hampton-based landscape designer Edwina von Gal, who, like Ries, has collaborated with the clients on other projects.

A Caribbean island is a challenging place to work under any circumstances. Everything has to be brought in from far away, including all the plants, which came by barge from Miami. St. Bart’s in particular requires anyone building to work with a local architect and engineer. In their initial proposal, this French team defaulted to that “slick and modernist” look, as von Gal describes it, with the oversized bedrooms and white color scheme that dominates much of the island’s luxury housing stock.

In a recent development, the design team pushed back—asking for a lot of bedrooms (eight) and generous living spaces. They also had strong opinions on the building materials. Given the island’s climate, the humid, salt-soaked air can be hard on everything. “If we did white paint, which is prominent throughout St. Bart's, it’s constant maintenance, constant painting,” notes Ries. The design team insisted on cladding the buildings in Ipe, the durable tropical hardwood, which wears well. It mystified the local architects and set the complex apart from its neighbors. It also makes the buildings disappear into the greenery of the hillside.

Sources indicate that but the architects quickly caught on to the newly introduced intends, and von Gal is eager to praise their technical accomplishments. Regulations require properties to conserve rainwater, so there are cisterns beneath the buildings, plus technology infrastructure and laundry facilities. “Working on the hill is so complex,” she says. “It's such a tight little package of technology and function. What they did was amazing.”.

The team decided to reconfigure the property as a series of pavilions that face the view of the ocean and surrounding hills. The main entry is at the top of the steep hill, along with parking. The next level down is for family bedrooms; below that is a primary suite and study; and finally the fourth level is the main living space, including a playroom. “We made sure this playroom was front and center,” says Ries. “My client loves her grandkids.”.

The playroom and study have built-in daybeds that can be used as spare guest rooms in a pinch. But the clients did get their eight bedrooms. “We know how to make compact bedrooms and make them very efficient, make them very livable, which allows us to fit in a lot of space for a lot of guests, and then that puts a lot of emphasis on having main entertaining spaces that are significant and gracious,” states Ries. “The idea is that everybody hangs out together.”.

Everything is united by generous outdoor spaces, which wind between the bedrooms. “Every room has an amazing view,” indicates Ries. “It feels almost like your own little treehouse in a way.” The bottom living area opens out to a pool and an expansive deck where the family eats most of their meals.

The house has an elevator, but stairs are the primary way the family moves between levels and finally down to the beach. “We hung on for a really great, gracious, fun set of stairs,” states von Gal. “They really introduce you to how amazing the different levels are and all the wonderful secret places.”.

Durable fabrics and materials were chosen throughout and Ries made sure everything could be easily moved around and reconfigured. Outside on the main deck, three long dining tables from Sutherland were outfitted with casters so they could be maneuvered into a single long table or several smaller ones; 26 lightweight dining chairs can be pulled from different parts of the deck. If the infamous “Christmas winds” bring a downpour, the tables can even be moved indoors so a dinner party can proceed in inclement weather. Outdoor seating can be arranged as a 15-foot sofa or several love seats.

“It's so flexible,” says Ries. “We know this from working with a client that their needs for entertaining change every day, or sometimes a couple times a day.”.

The kitchen is also efficient, designed to produce easy, clean meals. The family would rather spend time in the pool than over a stove. And no part of the living room is oriented around a TV. “They're readers,” states Ries. “There’s always stacks of new books when you go to their homes. So there’s all these cool little spots you can tuck into.”.

In a recent development, ultimately, the client and design team’s insistence on what they wanted paid off—but it wasn’t without a few moments of doubt. “When so many people are telling you ‘no, surely this is not what you want,’ it does start to erode your confidence a little,” says von Gal. “Then when it does come out well, there’s a real sense of triumph and satisfaction.”.

#134883. Tech Report: What to Eat for Healthier Skin and Slower Aging

📅 20 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 11m • 📚 Deep Dive (2106 w)
